title: We Are Not Having This Argument Again
gist_ar: خلاف حقيقي غير مكتوب: جمل مش مكمّلة، مقاطعات، والموضوع الحقيقي مش اللي بيتقال.

before_listening.en: A real argument between colleagues: unfinished sentences, people talking over each other. What it is actually about is never named.
before_listening.ar: خلاف حقيقي بين زمايل: جمل ناقصة وكلام فوق كلام. الموضوع الحقيقي عمره ما اتسمّى.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: —no, because you did the same thing in the October meeting, and I let it go.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: Did what? Say what the thing is. Because you keep saying 'the thing' and I—

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: You answered a question that was put to me. That's the thing. Sabah asked me what the timeline was and you answered it.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: Because I had the date in front of me and you were—

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: I was reaching for it. I had it open. There was a two-second gap and you filled it, and now it's in the minutes as your answer, and that is the third time.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: Right, okay, so this is about the minutes.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: It is absolutely not about the minutes.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: Then I honestly don't know what— because if the information was right, and it was right, then I'm struggling to see the damage. Tell me the damage.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: The damage is that Sabah has now asked you three times running and hasn't asked me once, and I don't think you did that on purpose, Bilal, I've never said you did it on purpose — but I'm going to be in a room in April defending a timeline that everyone in the building associates with you.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: And now you're doing the silence, which is the other thing.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: No — no, I'm not doing anything, I'm thinking, give me a second. ... The April thing hadn't occurred to me. That's, I mean, that's a bit uncomfortable to hear, because I've been telling myself I was covering for you. Which is a very nice way to describe taking something off somebody.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: It's a very nice way to describe it, yes.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: Fine. So what do you want me to do, practically? Because 'be more aware' is going to last me about four days.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: Count. When a question goes to me, count to five in your head. And if I'm still hunting for the file at five, say 'Samira, do you want me to take it?' — out loud, so it's a handover and not a substitution.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: ...That's mildly humiliating and completely reasonable. Yes. Alright.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: And the October one I'm letting go properly this time, not the way I let it go before.

segments.speaker: Bilal
segments.text: Which was not letting it go.

segments.speaker: Samira
segments.text: Which was not letting it go at all, no.

gist_question.q: What is the argument really about?
options: Whether the timeline recorded in the minutes is factually accurate and complete
Who will attend the meeting in April
Whether Bilal should have been at the October meeting
Whose work Sabah credits, and therefore who will be asked in future

questions.q: What concrete change do they agree on?
options: Bilal will stop attending any meetings that Sabah is also present at
Bilal will count to five and then offer the handover out loud
Samira will circulate the timeline before each meeting
The minutes will be rewritten to credit Samira

questions.q: What does Bilal realise about his own account of his behaviour?
options: That he had the wrong date in front of him after all
That he had been asked by Sabah to answer on her behalf
That 'covering for her' was a flattering description of taking something from her
That he was repeating something he learned in October

questions.q: Why does Samira insist it is 'absolutely not about the minutes'?
options: Because the minutes are only the record of a pattern she is objecting to
Because the minutes were never circulated
Because she wrote the minutes herself
Because Bilal is not named in the minutes

questions.q: What does Samira mean by distinguishing 'a handover' from 'a substitution'?
options: In one she visibly gives the answer away; in the other it is simply taken
One is minuted and the other is not
One happens before the meeting, the other during it
One is permanent and the other temporary
